# ZEN-STD-4.3 — five mandatory gates. Every job is blocking: a red gate
# stops the merge, and gate 5 never runs from a branch.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  gate-static:
    name: "GATE-01 lint + typecheck"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint --if-present
      - run: npm run build --workspaces --if-present

  gate-security:
    name: "GATE-02 SAST + secret scan"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Secret scan
        run: docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.21.2 detect --source=/repo --no-git --redact --verbose --exit-code=1
      - name: Static analysis (SAST)
        run: docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/src" -w /src semgrep/semgrep:1.90.0 semgrep scan --config p/default --metrics=off --error --quiet

  gate-test:
    name: "GATE-03 tests + contracts + coverage"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Contract lint (OpenAPI 3.1)
        if: ${{ hashFiles('contracts/openapi/*.v1.yaml') != '' }}
        run: npx --yes @redocly/cli@1.25.0 lint contracts/openapi/*.v1.yaml
      - name: Event schemas are valid JSON Schema
        if: ${{ hashFiles('contracts/events/*.json') != '' }}
        run: node scripts/validate-event-schemas.mjs
      - run: npm run test --workspaces --if-present
      - name: Coverage threshold
        if: ${{ hashFiles('**/test/**/*.test.*', '**/tests/**/*.py') != '' }}
        run: npx --yes c8@10.1.3 --check-coverage --lines 80 --reporter=text-summary npm run test --workspaces --if-present

  gate-image:
    name: "GATE-04 image build + scan"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: gate-test
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        service: [gateway, users, orders, notifications]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Resolve the service folder
        id: svc
        run: |
          name='${{ matrix.service }}'
          if [ -d "services/$name" ]; then
            echo "dir=services/$name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "dir=services/${name^}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -f ${{ steps.svc.outputs.dir }}/Dockerfile -t ${{ matrix.service }}:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Scan image
        run: docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock aquasec/trivy:0.56.2 image --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed ${{ matrix.service }}:${{ github.sha }}

  gate-deploy:
    name: "GATE-05 deploy (manual approval)"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [gate-static, gate-security, gate-test, gate-image]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Record the approved build
        run: echo "approved ${{ github.sha }} — no manifests to roll out"

# AGENTS.md — demo-app

Test project

Read this before your first edit. The block between the `zen-standards` comments is
generated from the ZEN engineering standard and is rewritten when the scaffold is
regenerated — put your own notes outside it.

<!-- zen-standards:begin -->
## ZEN engineering standards (binding)

Every change must keep these clauses true. If a clause cannot be satisfied, say so in
the response instead of working around it — the CI gates will reject the change anyway.

### Runtime (handbook §4.2)

| Clause | Rule | Where it is already true |
|---|---|---|
| `ZEN-STD-CON-01` | Containers are multi-stage, run as a non-root user, declare a HEALTHCHECK and pin their base image to an exact version. | `services/*/Dockerfile` |
| `ZEN-STD-CON-02` | Contract first: no route exists without a document in `contracts/`, every service is served under `/api/v1`, events use one versioned envelope. | `contracts/openapi/*.v1.yaml`, `contracts/events/*.json` |
| `ZEN-STD-CON-03` | Logs are one JSON object per line on stdout, `/metrics` exposes Prometheus text, and `X-Correlation-ID` is reused or minted once at the edge and forwarded. | `packages/shared/src/logger.ts`, `correlation.ts`, `metrics.ts` |
| `ZEN-STD-CON-04` | `/healthz/live` reports the process, `/healthz/ready` reports the dependency check and withdraws before shutdown; SIGTERM drains in-flight work. | `packages/shared/src/health.ts`, `lifecycle.ts` |
| `ZEN-STD-CON-05` | JWTs are validated at the edge, secrets come from the environment or a secret store, and nothing credential-shaped is committed. | `.env.example` (placeholders only), `deploy/k8s/*-secrets.yaml` (empty `stringData`) |
| `ZEN-STD-CON-06` | Every outbound call has a timeout, bounded retries with jitter and a circuit breaker; writes accept and honour an `Idempotency-Key`. | `packages/shared/src/resilience.ts` (timeout, retry, breaker, idempotency) |

### CI (handbook §4.3) — a red gate blocks the merge

| Clause | Rule | Where it is already true |
|---|---|---|
| `ZEN-STD-CI-01` | Lint + typecheck, secret scan (gitleaks) and SAST (Semgrep) must be clean — GATE-01 and GATE-02. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · jobs `gate-static`, `gate-security` |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-02` | Unit tests, contract lint (Redocly) and event-schema validation must pass with coverage at or above the gate — GATE-03. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · job `gate-test`, `scripts/validate-event-schemas.mjs` |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-03` | Every service image must build from the committed Dockerfile; a build that only works locally is a red gate. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · job `gate-image` (build step) |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-04` | The built image is scanned and fails on HIGH or CRITICAL findings — GATE-04. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · job `gate-image` (Trivy step) |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-05` | Deployment runs only from `main` after all four gates pass and only against the `production` environment — GATE-05. | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` · job `deploy` |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-06` | A service that needs a store gets its own database — no shared schema, no cross-service table reads. | `docker-compose.databases.yml` (one Postgres per domain service) |
| `ZEN-STD-CI-07` | Manifests declare resources, run non-root with a read-only root filesystem, and probe the paths the app actually serves. | `deploy/k8s/*.yaml` (ConfigMap, Secret, Deployment, Service) |

### Repository layout (handbook §4.1, amended for a monorepo)

- `services/<name>/` — one deployable per domain service; no service reads another's tables.
- `services/gateway/` — the only process exposed to clients; it forwards `/api/v1/*` verbatim.
- `contracts/` — OpenAPI document per service plus one JSON Schema per published event.
- `packages/shared/` — code every TypeScript service compiles in; never a runtime dependency between services.
- `deploy/k8s/`, `docker-compose.yml` — deployment surface; the database overlay is opt-in.

### What an agent must not do here

- Invent a service, route or event without adding its contract to `contracts/` in the same change.
- Call another service over the network without a timeout, or retry a non-idempotent write.
- Edit `contracts/`, the CI workflow or a Dockerfile to make a red gate pass.
- Commit a credential, or pin a base image to `latest`.

### Project structure

Services: gateway, users, orders, notifications
Gateway: gateway
Stack: node-ts

<!-- zen-standards:end -->

## Build & Test

Install, run and test from the repository root — the exact commands per package are in
`README.md`. The commands CI runs are the ones to trust: `npm test`.
files.ARCHITECTURE.md:
# demo-app — microservices architecture

Test project

## Service catalog

| Service | Folder | Port | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gateway | `services/gateway` | 4000 | single entry point, routes traffic to domain services |
| users | `services/users` | 4001 | domain service (owns its own data) |
| orders | `services/orders` | 4002 | domain service (owns its own data) |
| notifications | `services/notifications` | 4003 | domain service (owns its own data) |

## Shared contracts

`packages/shared` (`@demo-app/shared`) holds DTOs, event envelopes and the health payload. It is
versioned with the repo and consumed as a workspace dependency — never copy types between services.

## Rules

1. **One deployable per folder.** A service never imports another service's source; cross-service calls go
   through HTTP or the broker.
2. **Data ownership.** Each service owns its store; no shared database schema.
3. **Contracts first.** Change `@demo-app/shared` before changing producers/consumers, and keep events backward compatible.
4. **Failure isolation.** Every service exposes liveness (`/healthz/live`), readiness
   (`/healthz/ready`) and a Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint. Every outbound call goes
   through the shared resilience kit - never an inline `setTimeout` or a bare `await`
   on a network call. The rule table below names the symbol behind each obligation.
5. **Async by default.** Use the nats broker for side effects (notifications, projections) and HTTP only for request/response.
6. **Single entry point.** Clients talk to `gateway` only; it maps `/api/v1/<service>` prefixes to service URLs (see `services/gateway/src/index.ts`).

## Resilience rules

Every obligation below is implemented in `packages/shared/src/resilience.ts` — import
it from the shared package; do not hand-roll a timeout or a retry loop.

| Obligation | Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| Every outbound call has a 2-3s timeout. | `withTimeout` - defaults to RESILIENCE_DEFAULTS.timeoutMs (2500ms) and aborts the signal it hands you |
| Retries are bounded and back off exponentially with jitter. | `retry` - RESILIENCE_DEFAULTS.attempts attempts, full jitter over min(2000ms, 100ms * 2^attempt) |
| A failing dependency is cut off instead of queued against. | `CircuitBreaker` - opens after 5 consecutive failures, half-open probe after 10000ms |
| Non-idempotent writes are keyed with Idempotency-Key. | `IdempotencyGuard` - one effect per key, concurrent duplicates share the in-flight call, a changed payload with the same key is a 409 |

## Local development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev --workspaces --if-present
```

Or the whole stack in containers:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

# Contracts — demo-app

The contract is the source of truth. Change a document here **before** you change
the implementation; a pull request that changes a component, a route or an event
payload without touching this folder is incomplete.

## Layout

| Service | OpenAPI | Publishes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | `contracts/openapi/users.v1.yaml` | `user.created`, `user.updated` |
| `orders` | `contracts/openapi/orders.v1.yaml` | `order.created`, `order.updated` |
| `notifications` | `contracts/openapi/notifications.v1.yaml` | `notification.created`, `notification.updated` |

- `openapi/` — one OpenAPI 3.1.0 document per service, versioned in the file name (`.v1.yaml`).
- `events/` — `envelope.v1.json` plus one JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) per event. Schemas are self-contained: each restates the envelope and pins `eventType`.

Every service router is mounted under `/api/v1`, so a route described here as
`/api/v1/users` is reachable at exactly that path.
`/health` is the only path outside the prefix — the Dockerfile
`HEALTHCHECK` and the orchestrator probes depend on it.

## Rules

1. **Additive changes only within a version.** Adding an optional field is fine;
   removing or retyping one requires a new version (`.v2`) and a migration note.
2. **Events are facts in the past tense.** `order.created`, not `createOrder`.
   Consumers ignore unknown fields, so new optional payload fields are safe.
3. **Never publish a payload you have not described here.** The envelope's
   `eventId` is the deduplication key for at-least-once delivery.
4. **Lint before you push** — the CI contract gate runs:

```bash
npx @redocly/cli lint openapi/*.v1.yaml
```

## Generated

These files are emitted by the project template. They are meant to be edited —
that is the point of contract-first — but keep the version in the file name in
step with the version in the document.

# One database per service — ZEN-STD-4.3 data ownership.
#
# No shared schema and no shared credentials: every service gets its own
# database, its own role and its own volume. The base compose file stays
# database-free, so this overlay is opt-in:
#
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.databases.yml up
#   # or: export COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker-compose.databases.yml
#
services:
  users-db:
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: users
      POSTGRES_USER: users
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${USERS_DB_PASSWORD:-localonly}
    ports:
      - "5433:5432"
    volumes:
      - users-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U users -d users"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  users:
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://users:${USERS_DB_PASSWORD:-localonly}@users-db:5432/users
    depends_on:
      users-db:
        condition: service_healthy

  orders-db:
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: orders
      POSTGRES_USER: orders
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${ORDERS_DB_PASSWORD:-localonly}
    ports:
      - "5434:5432"
    volumes:
      - orders-db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U orders -d orders"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  orders:

    depends_on:
      notifications-db:

files.README.md:
# demo-app

Test project

Workspace tooling: **npm** · Services: `gateway`, `users`, `orders`, `notifications`

Message broker: **nats** (`nats://localhost:4222`)

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev --workspaces --if-present
```

Everything in containers:

```bash
docker compose up --build
docker compose down
```

## Layout

```
package.json          workspaces: services/*, packages/*
tsconfig.base.json    shared TypeScript config
services/
  gateway/           src/index.ts, Dockerfile
  users/           src/index.ts, Dockerfile
  orders/           src/index.ts, Dockerfile
  notifications/           src/index.ts, Dockerfile
packages/shared/      contracts, health, broker
docker-compose.yml    local stack
ARCHITECTURE.md       service boundaries and rules
```

## Scripts

| Script | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `build` | npm run build --workspaces --if-present |
| `dev` | npm run dev --workspaces --if-present |
| `test` | npm run test --workspaces --if-present |
| `docker:up` | `docker compose up --build` |
| `docker:down` | `docker compose down` |

Every service listens on its own port and exposes `/healthz/live` (liveness),
`/healthz/ready` (readiness) and `/metrics` (Prometheus).

# Build from the repo root: docker build -f services/gateway/Dockerfile .
FROM node:20.18.0-alpine3.20 AS build
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY package*.json ./
COPY tsconfig*.json ./
COPY packages ./packages
COPY services ./services
RUN npm install
RUN npm run build --workspace @demo-app/shared && npm run build --workspace @demo-app/gateway

FROM node:20.18.0-alpine3.20 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV PORT=4000
COPY --from=build /workspace/services/gateway/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /workspace/node_modules ./node_modules
# Non-root: the official node image already ships a `node` user (uid 1000).
USER node
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --retries=3 --start-period=10s CMD wget -q --spider http://127.0.0.1:4000/health || exit 1
EXPOSE 4000
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
